meta.title_plain: How Andre Agassi fell to No. 141 and climbed back to No. 1
meta.teaser: Andre Agassi dropped to No. 141, then rebuilt his game in small tournaments and reached No. 1.

page.title: How Andre Agassi fell to No. 141 and climbed back to No. 1
page.bigIdea: Andre Agassi was a star who fell almost out of sight. He came back by starting small and working hard, and won more than ever.

cards.title: A court in the backyard
cards.front: Andre was born in 1970 in Las Vegas, USA.
cards.back: His dad, a former Olympic boxer, built a tennis court in their backyard. By age 2, Andre could already serve a ball over a full court.
cards.tryit: Hit 20 serves today and count how many land in. Write the number down.

cards.title: Off to academy at 13
cards.front: At 13, Andre moved to a tennis academy in Florida.
cards.back: He trained at Nick Bollettieri's academy and turned pro at just 16, in 1986. His big, powerful forehand made people notice him fast.
cards.tryit: Hit 15 forehands and focus only on a smooth follow-through over your shoulder.

cards.title: Flashy star at the top
cards.front: In 1992, Andre won his first Grand Slam at Wimbledon.
cards.back: Then he won the 1994 US Open and the 1995 Australian Open. In April 1995, he became world No. 1 for the first time.
cards.tryit: Write down one big tennis goal and one small step toward it this week.

cards.title: The fall to No. 141
cards.front: By November 1997, Andre was ranked No. 141.
cards.back: A wrist injury kept hurting his play, and he lost focus. Many people said his career at the top was over.
cards.tryit: Think of a time you played badly. Write one thing you learned from it.

cards.title: Starting small to rise
cards.front: In 1998, Andre went back to the small tournaments.
cards.back: He trained hard on fitness and played lower 'Challenger' events. He climbed from No. 110 to No. 6 in one year, then reached No. 1 again in 1999.
cards.tryit: Do a 10-minute fitness set: shuttle runs, side steps and jump rope.

words.d: One of tennis's four biggest tournaments, like Wimbledon or the French Open.
A smaller pro tournament, one level below the main tour.
The shot you hit back when your opponent serves.
Winning all four Grand Slam tournaments at least once.
Returning to success after a time of losing or struggling.

quiz.q: How low did Andre's ranking fall in 1997?
quiz.hint: Look at card 4. It was well outside the top 100.
quiz.why: A wrist injury and lost focus dropped him to No. 141 in November 1997.

quiz.q: What did Andre do in 1998 to come back?
opts: Played small Challenger events and trained hard
quiz.why: He worked on fitness and played lower-level events to rebuild, rising to No. 6.

quiz.q: In the 1999 French Open final, Andre was two sets down. What happened?
quiz.hint: That title gave him all four Grand Slams.
quiz.why: He came back from two sets down to win, completing his career Grand Slam.

quiz.q: Andre was nicknamed 'the Punisher'. Which shot was he famous for?
quiz.hint: It's the first shot you hit when the other player serves.
quiz.why: He punished serves by hitting returns early and hard, putting rivals on defence.

page.think: Andre went back to small tournaments to rebuild. If your tennis ever hit a slump, what 'small tournament' step could you take to climb back?
